ccp2014br.title: The Bloodbath of B-R5RB, Gaming's Most Destructive Battle Ever
ccp2014br.author: CCP Dolan
ccp2014br.quote: With the length and intensity of this fight however, this slowdown was not enough to completely cover it, so it hit our limit of running the simulation at 10% of normal time. Consequently, over the 21 hours players experienced of the fight, the server was put to task to run just over 2 hours worth of simulation.
quotes: In the early hours of January 27 th , 2014 CONCORD (the NPC “police force”) came to collect the sovereignty bill for a dead-end system in the Immensea region called B-R5RB.

One of over 7,500 in game, this particular system – with its 9 planets, 66 moons and 12 asteroid belts – had recently been transferred to a player corporation called H A V O C , a corp used by the alliance Pandemic Legion to handle sovereignty transfers between Alliances
they found that H A V O C had left their automatic payment unchecked. Without the necessary payment, sovereignty in the system immediately dropped leaving the system up for grabs.

Around 21 hours of total fighting · 7,548 unique characters belonging to those two coalitions participated in the overall battle (i.e. landed on at least one killmail). 6,058 participated directly in the B-R5RB system with 2,670 in system at max
Titans – 75 (74 in system, one on its way to the fight)

Supercarriers – 13 (12 in system, one as it tried to escape the system) · Dreadnaughts – 370 (356 in system, 14 in connected skirmishes as both sides attempted to stop the other from bringing reinforcements) · Carriers – 123
11 TRILLION ISK. According to some PLEX conversions that could equate to approximately $300,000-$330,000 USD.

Due to how we set up our universe, the effect of this slowdown is localized, often applying to just the problematic system and allowing the vast majority of other online players to continue on as happy as can be blowing up ships, mining, trading, exploring etc as long as they didn’t come near these massive fights.
This wasn’t the largest single battle in terms of numbers of participants in system at once. That record still belongs to the battle for 6VDT-H, which reached 4,070 pilots in system.
ccp2014br.note: First-party after-action report published on eveonline.com; byline on the page is '2014-02-01 - By CCP Dolan'. Classified 'postmortem' because it is the operator's own account of the incident and of how the cluster degraded under it (the 'Time Dilation' section). The same page closes with marketing copy, so every figure here is CCP's own, not independently audited; the USD number is CCP's PLEX conversion.
supports: 21 hours of fighting, just over 2 hours of simulation

tidi2011.title: Introducing Time Dilation (TiDi)
tidi2011.author: CCP Veritas
tidi2011.quote: Time dilation does not solve everything. Some load is not tied to a time duration, so we won't be able to handle indefinitely-sized fights.
quotes: The EVE Online server should degrade in such a way that the queue of tasklets waiting for execution is minimized - ideally zero.
In order to bring things down to the level where the server can keep up, there's painfully few options. They boil down to two: reduce load or increase processing capacity.
Going multi-threaded falls into the increasing capacity category - it increases how much load can be processed per second, but never as much as most people think.
It's often said that the War on Lag cannot be won because our players can always bring one more ship.
tidi2011.note: The design blog that announced TiDi, written by the Team Gridlock engineer who built it. Published 2011-04-22; the feature shipped later. Dev blog, so a first-hand account but not a peer-reviewed or incident-report source.
supports: Time Dilation was designed as graceful degradation, not a fix
the ceiling was stated in advance
only two options: reduce load or increase capacity

ccpfleet2016.title: Fleet Fight Notifications & You!
ccpfleet2016.author: CCP Falcon
ccpfleet2016.quote: The Fleet Fight notification system is completely automated, and only reinforces the actual solar system that is requested.
quotes: we've been watching the fleet fight notification system and would like to clarify how it should be used to maximum effect in order that the correct nodes are properly reinforced
If an attacking fleet needs the full constellation reinforced, they need to have their leader submit an individual fleet fight notification for each of the other systems in that constellation too.
ccpfleet2016.note: CCP's own description of node reinforcement: the granularity of the request, and therefore of the hardware CCP allocates, is one solar system, filed by players in advance. The post says nothing about how many solar systems share a node.
supports: hardware reinforcement is granted one solar system at a time, on request

unverified: That B-R5RB's simulation ran on exactly one process pinned to one CPU core. CCP's public sources say the slowdown is localized to the problematic system and that reinforcement is granted per solar system, but no CCP source opened here states a one-system-one-core mapping.

Any one-solar-system-per-node mapping, and whether reinforcement worked in January 2014 as CCP describes it in 2016. The only opened source is CCP Falcon's 2016-03-31 post, which says the system 'only reinforces the actual solar system that is requested' and nothing about how many systems share a node; the story claims only the reinforcement granularity, and never as a claim about that night.

The end date of the battle, commonly given as 28 January 2014. CCP's report dates only the start ('the early hours of January 27 th , 2014') and says daily server maintenance downtime ended the conflict.
That CCP has never since solved single-solar-system scaling. No source opened here makes that claim in those terms, so the story does not.
The identity of any individual director responsible for the missed bill. CCP's report attributes it to the corporation H A V O C leaving 'their automatic payment unchecked' and names no person.
Any independent (non-CCP) valuation of the destroyed ships in USD. The $300,000-$330,000 range is CCP's own PLEX conversion.

That EVE's engine requires everything in a solar system to see everything else, in order. No CCP source opened here states it; the story and card c4 argue it from what a shared simulation has to do, not from a document. It is the story's reasoning, not reportage.
